thread:
ashley: Heads up — after last night's quantized model deploy I'm seeing a spike in KV cache evictions and a couple of OOMs on worker-gpu-7. Hit-rate dropped ~20%. Can we triage prefix cache keying + eviction/TTL behavior quickly?

matt: Do we have profiling traces? I want to see KV sizes and fragmentation patterns. Might be kernel selection changes interacting with batching.

ashley: Attaching a short extract from the trace (copied):
```
[2024-04-05T02:11:03Z] worker-gpu-7: cache.entries=14512 cache.size_bytes=13.9GB evictions=1825 OOM_events=1
[2024-04-05T02:11:08Z] batching.window=4ms avg_batch=12 seq_len=1024
[2024-04-05T02:11:10Z] kernel=opt_attn_v2 fallback=matmul64 latency_p95=210ms
```

liam: Noted. Quick theory: quantization changed tokenization alignment for a subset of requests so prefix normalization that used raw prompt string is missing canonicalization. We ended up with many near-duplicate keys differing by whitespace/metadata. Hit-rate drops a lot from that.

matt: That aligns with the profile — lots of small entries (few KB each) but many duplicates. Cache fragmentation up, effective usable buffer shrank. Suggest two short fixes: 1) normalize keys (strip/normalize whitespace + collapse metadata fields) then hash (sha1) and cap key length. 2) change eviction to size-aware LRU so large entries don't evict many small ones spuriously.

sara: Also consider TTL tuning: the current TTL is 6h for prefix cache. For common prefixes that rarely change, keep longer; for user-provided noisy prefixes shorten to 30m. We can implement a two-tier TTL: static_prefix_ttl and dynamic_prefix_ttl with a fast heuristic.

perf-bot: perf summary for last 24h:
- overall hit-rate: 68% -> 52% after deploy
- avg token cost per request: +12%
- observed GPU memory fragmentation: medium
- top eviction cause: LRU by recency (not size)

ashley: Plan: roll a canary with 3 changes: canonicalize and sha1 keying, enable size-aware LRU (evict entries to free <= 1GB increments), and two-tier TTL (static 12h, dynamic 30m). Warmup strategy: at model load, prefill top 200 prefixes observed in the last week to avoid cold starts.

matt: I'll run the canary on 3% traffic. Metrics I'll watch: hit-rate, p95 latency, evictions/sec, OOMs. If warmup adds <5ms tail latency we're good.

liam: For key canonicalization here's a tiny snippet we used before:
```python
def canonical_key(prompt):
    p = prompt.strip()
    p = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", p)
    p = remove_user_metadata(p)
    return sha1(p.encode()).hexdigest()[:40]
```

ashley: Good. Also watch kernel selection telemetry — if opt_attn_v2 fallback rate increases with batching, we may need to bias routing to different kernel or shorter batches for those model slices.

sara: I'll tweak TTL rules and add a config flag for size-aware eviction threshold.

matt: Starting canary now. pinging in #incidents if anything spikes.

ashley: Awesome. :thumbsup: We'll regroup after 6h with perf snapshots and decide on rollout.
